narrative.overview:
Green is information, not decoration. The interface is built from deep neutral surfaces and dense, readable rows, with Signal Green reserved for the moments that mean something: someone is online, a message is unread, a chat is selected, an action is available. When the green appears, it has a job. When it does not, the system falls back to carbon-grey tonal steps and hairline separators rather than reaching for ornament.

The mood is calm, utilitarian, and quietly confident. This is a long-running desktop tool, so density and legibility outrank flourish: a 15px body, tight 8–16px rhythm, generous use of 12–16px radii to soften an otherwise rectangular workspace, and motion that resolves almost before you notice it. Skeuomorphism, playful confetti, and marketing-page flourish are explicit visual rejections; the product’s performance and privacy story is carried by restraint, not by spectacle.

Light and dark are peers, not an afterthought. Every surface, text, and bubble token has a dark counterpart, and the two canvases share the same geometry and motion. A legacy runtime customiser (theme.config.ts + applyThemeColors) can override individual colour keys at runtime; the values in the frontmatter are the declared @theme baseline.
keyCharacteristics: Signal-led: one accent, used only for live, selected, or actionable states.
Dense but breathable: 15px body, 8–16px rhythm, 12–16px radii.
Dual-canvas: every token has a light and dark expression.
Flat at rest: tonal steps and hairline borders do the structural work.
Restrained motion: state changes finish within a few hundred milliseconds.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Green appears only where something is live, selected, or actionable. Decoration never gets the green.

rules.name: The Two-Canvas Rule
rules.body: No new colour enters the system without its dark-mode counterpart. A token with one expression is an incomplete token.

rules.name: The Single-Voice Rule
rules.body: One family, one weight ladder. A second font appears only inside code spans; never for headings, never for emphasis.

rules.name: The Quiet Layer Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a shadow is doing structural work on a permanent surface, use a tonal step or a hairline border instead.

rules.name: The Restrained Motion Rule
rules.body: State changes resolve within 300ms — menus 160ms, slides and toasts 220ms, bubbles 180ms. The toggle’s 600ms elastic slide is the deliberate exception, not a precedent.

dos: Do keep Signal Green to live, selected, or actionable states, per The Signal Rule.
Do pair every new token with a light and dark expression, per The Two-Canvas Rule.
Do keep body copy at 15px/1.5 and let 13px and 11px carry only metadata.
Do use alpha hairlines (8% white in dark mode) for permanent separators.
Do keep conversation bubbles within 85% width, tightening to 65% at `lg`.
Do extend the `@theme` block in `style.css` when adding a token, then check `theme.config.ts` for a runtime override of the same key.
donts: Don’t use the accent as section decoration, background wash, or large fill.
Don’t add resting shadows to cards, rows, or panels; see The Quiet Layer Rule.
Don’t introduce a second typeface outside inline code; see The Single-Voice Rule.
Don’t let a new colour ship with only one theme’s value.
Don’t exceed the established motion budget; the toggle’s spring is the sole exception.
Don’t set one-off colours in components when a token belongs in `@theme`.
